$comment: Per-file allowances for scripts/ci/check_fabricated_facts.py. A count may fall and may never rise; a file absent here may have none. Every rule records the owner accountable for retiring its remainder and the date by which that must happen - an expired allowance fails the check, which is what stops a ratchet becoming permanent.

fabricated_observation_literal.reason: Two cases remain. state/constants.rs declares LEGACY_UNRECORDED_AT, the v1 wire compatibility sentinel for historical Session events without a durable time; a versioned read must preserve the underlying unknown observation. official_request_witnesses.rs builds a synthetic pagination cursor whose created_at is a cursor position, not a record's observation. The Models API now reads Control's durable local publication time through the existing Coordinator registration history.

ambient_clock_read.reason: The wall clock predates the WallClock port across the worker, runtime and control tiers. Each file is converted by taking a WallClock at construction or the caller's sampled instant as an argument; the count may only fall. The scan was widened to Utc::now, concrete clock values read in place (SystemClock.now_ms(), Clock::now_ms(&SystemClock)), cfg(any(test, feature)) code that ships with its feature, and files that declare their own clock trait (no longer exempt); that raised the recorded 167 reads in 97 files to 190 in 110 without any new read being written. The model-request budget and retry work then added three (provider-genai, the runtime inference engine), and the BOOTTIME authority clock moved local-process's read into awaken-authority-clock: 193 in 110. Run ingress, the container sandbox's waits and warm pool, the Worker's registration and evidence loops and the Session application now read monotonic time through awaken_lease_contract::mono (Stopwatch, MonoDeadline) and wall time through their injected clock; what remains in the Worker lifecycle is paired with the BOOTTIME authority proof's scheduling Instant, and the container effect-fence and egress reads wait on the runtime-host composition that builds those providers. The Managed adapter's rate limit, Skill, Memory-store, Deployment and Work routes and its projection timings read the Resources, Deployment, Session or Coordinator clock they are composed with, and the Deployment application stamps on its injected clock. Every remaining monotonic reading outside the Worker lifecycle's authority proof and the model-inference clock (the OAuth token cache, MCP progress throttling, the circuit breaker, tool timing, image-build and shutdown waits, the FUSE drain and content cache, Dream and evaluation timings) now goes through awaken_lease_contract::mono. The Coordinator's application access (issuance, revocation, expiry, retention), fleet readiness, claim-fenced Artifact publication, claimed commits, operator quarantine and Dream processes stamp and judge on the Coordinator clock they are composed with. The Runtime's and the native provider's inference timing read mono instead of the retired TokioModelInferenceClock. The container provider and the Kubernetes runtime judge effect fences and issue allowlist capabilities on the clock the execution composition installs (fail closed without one), and the runtime owner id is a random incarnation nonce rather than a time. The authority proof's scheduling half is a mono instant, so the Worker lifecycle's renewal pacing and latency read mono; the proof's authority half stays the BOOTTIME sample in awaken-authority-clock, the only reading compared with the physical cutoff. Control's IAM adapters (embedded, remote and the enforce engine), the admin config surfaces, Repository credential validation, Managed Agent lifecycle stamps and model publication take the process clock from the Control component; audit call identities and Agent ids are random, and registration lag is a mono elapsed. Captured content stamps and erasure fences read the Coordinator's clock; the Resource Worker routes judge claims and leases on the Coordinator's clock; a FUSE Memory projection stamps its mount on the clock its mounter was composed with; the Hand judges request deadlines and the Git credential helper judges capability expiry on the clock the Sandbox process's main chooses; the check-directory nonce is random. Worker observation/cleanup/drain now use the process clock; fallback and Credential IDs use the canonical random incarnation; retry jitter uses standard entropy rather than time (23 -> 19 ambient reads). The Resources Skill catalog now stamps authored versions from the ResourceAuthorities clock (19 -> 18). The CLI Runtime capability query and startup/recurring Resource reclamation now sample the already composed process or Resources clock (18 -> 15). Web Search and Fetch publication now judge exact credential expiry on the composed process clock (15 -> 14). Memory Extraction now stamps and judges every claim transition on the Host process clock passed to its controller (14 -> 13). Credential mutation and materialization now use their composing Control/Worker clock through the existing fence, admission and recovery paths (13 -> 11). The Memory content repositories now take the Resources process clock, preserving full nanoseconds and checked SQL range (11 -> 10). The Host now injects the one process clock into the BackgroundTask supervisor for submission, ownership and renewal (10 -> 9). The Cloud brokered catalog now stamps successful refreshes on the composing CLI process clock (9 -> 8). Coordinator Environment image-build demand, claim, completion and retry now read the injected process clock (8 -> 7). A2A config and delivery IDs now reuse the agent-contract random process namespace and sequence instead of two time-based generators (7 -> 5). A2A wire status timestamps now sample the Coordinator Host clock at each publication boundary (5 -> 4). ACP capability profiles now retain the Host observation instant instead of sampling an independent clock (4 -> 3). ACP Worker observations now use the composing process WallClock through the one resolver and preparation path (3 -> 2). CLI WorkspaceData startup admission and request-time lease guard now share the composing process WallClock (2 -> 1); the BOOTTIME physical authority sampler remains.
